# Code Snippet

A polished code block: rounded surface, optional window chrome, copy-on-hover, line numbers and token-driven highlighting. A small, dependency-free tokenizer covers TS/TSX, JSON, shell and CSS; plug in Shiki for every other language, in your theme's colors.

```tsx title="call-to-action.tsx"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"
import { ArrowRight } from "koala-icons"
export function CallToAction() {
  // The label is the affordance; the icon just clarifies it.
  return (
    <Button>
      Get started
      <ArrowRight className="size-4" />
    </Button>
  )
}
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli@latest init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli@latest add code-snippet
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/code-snippet/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
import { CodeSnippet } from "@/components/ui/code-snippet"

export function Example() {
  return <CodeSnippet lang="tsx" code={`const x = 1`} />
}
```

## Languages

Set `lang` to switch grammars. TS/TSX, shell (`bash`/`sh`), and CSS are highlighted; the language chip in the header reflects the choice.

## More languages

For Python, Go, SQL, YAML and the two hundred other languages Shiki knows, put a `CodeHighlighterProvider` above your snippets. A highlighter answers in Koala's token types, not colors, so Shiki paints with the same syntax tokens and follows all four themes. Nothing in Code Snippet imports Shiki: without the provider, the bundle is as small as before.

Install Shiki, add the adapter, and provide it once near the root of your app. Languages load the first time a snippet asks for one, on Shiki's JavaScript engine (no WASM).

```bash
npm install shiki
```

```ts title="lib/shiki-highlighter.ts"
import { createCssVariablesTheme, createHighlighterCore, type HighlighterCore } from "shiki/core"
import { createJavaScriptRegexEngine } from "shiki/engine/javascript"
import { bundledLanguages } from "shiki/langs"

import type { CodeHighlighter, CodeToken, CodeTokenType } from "@/lib/code-highlighter"

const theme = createCssVariablesTheme({ name: "koala", variablePrefix: "--shiki-" })

const ROLE: Record<string, CodeTokenType> = {
  "token-keyword": "keyword",
  "token-string": "string",
  "token-string-expression": "string",
  "token-link": "string",
  "token-comment": "comment",
  "token-function": "function",
  "token-constant": "number",
  "token-parameter": "attribute",
  "token-punctuation": "punctuation",
}

let core: Promise<HighlighterCore> | null = null
const loading = new Map<string, Promise<void>>()

function highlighter() {
  core ??= createHighlighterCore({ themes: [theme], langs: [], engine: createJavaScriptRegexEngine() })
  return core
}

export const shikiHighlighter: CodeHighlighter = async (code, lang) => {
  const load = bundledLanguages[lang as keyof typeof bundledLanguages]
  if (!load) return null
  const shiki = await highlighter()
  if (!shiki.getLoadedLanguages().includes(lang)) {
    if (!loading.has(lang)) loading.set(lang, load().then((mod) => shiki.loadLanguage(mod.default)))
    await loading.get(lang)
  }
  const { tokens } = shiki.codeToTokens(code, { lang, theme: "koala" })
  return tokens.map((line) =>
    line.map((token): CodeToken => {
      const role = /--shiki-([\w-]+)/.exec(token.color ?? "")?.[1]
      return { type: role ? ROLE[role] : undefined, value: token.content }
    }),
  )
}
```

```tsx title="app/providers.tsx"
"use client"

import { CodeHighlighterProvider } from "@/lib/code-highlighter"
import { shikiHighlighter } from "@/lib/shiki-highlighter"

export function Providers({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <CodeHighlighterProvider highlighter={shikiHighlighter}>{children}</CodeHighlighterProvider>
}
```

## Window chrome

A `filename` adds the header with a language chip; `dots` adds macOS-style window dots. With either, the snippet wears the inset look: the header sits on a tinted frame and the code is a sheet set 8px into it, its corners concentric with the frame's. Omit both for a chromeless block.

```tsx title="button.tsx"
export function Button() {
  return <button className="btn">Click me</button>
}
```

```tsx
export function Button() {
  return <button className="btn">Click me</button>
}
```

When the snippet is already a sheet inside another frame (a preview's Code tab), a second frame would double the chrome. Pass `inset={false}` and the header becomes a strip across the one surface instead.

```tsx title="button.tsx"
export function Button() {
  return <button className="btn">Click me</button>
}
```

## Terminal sessions

In a shell snippet, start a line with `$` and it reads as a session: the prompt dims, each line without one is the command's output, in muted ink with a leading ✓ kept green. The copy button copies only the commands, without their prompt, so what lands on the clipboard runs as pasted.

```bash title="Terminal"
$ npx koalaui-cli@latest add button
✓ wrote components/ui/button/button.tsx
✓ wrote components/ui/button/index.ts
✓ added button
```

## Line numbers

Set `showLineNumbers` to render a tabular-nums gutter, useful for longer listings or when referencing a specific line.

```tsx title="tokenize.ts"
export function tokenize(code: string) {
  const tokens = []
  for (const line of code.split("\n")) {
    tokens.push(line.trim())
  }
  return tokens
}
```

## Diff

Show a change in context. `startLine` numbers the gutter from the excerpt's real position in the file, and `diff` marks lines as added or removed by that same number. A marked line takes a soft success or destructive band across the code plus a bar in the gutter, so the mark never rests on color alone, and a screen reader hears “Added” or “Removed” before it. The copy button still copies the plain `code` string.

```ts title="auth/reset.ts"
export function buildResetLink(userId: string) {
  const token = signResetToken({ uid: userId })

  const baseUrl = "https://staging.example.com"
  const baseUrl = "https://example.com"

  const url = new URL("/reset-password", baseUrl)
  url.searchParams.set("token", token)
  return url.toString()
}
```

## Collapsible

Long listings get noisy. Set `collapsible` to clamp the block to `collapsedHeight` (320px by default): the last lines dissolve into a bottom fade and a *Show more* toggle expands it to full height, animated. The toggle only appears once the content actually overflows the clamp, measured from the DOM, so short blocks are left untouched.

```tsx title="members-table.tsx"
import * as React from "react"

import { tv } from "@/lib/tv"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"

type Member = {
  id: string
  name: string
  email: string
  status: "Active" | "Invited" | "Suspended"
  balance: number
}

const columns: ColumnDef<Member>[] = [
  {
    accessorKey: "name",
    header: "Member",
    cell: ({ row }) => (
      <TableCellText primary={row.original.name} secondary={row.original.email} />
    ),
  },
  {
    accessorKey: "status",
    header: "Status",
    cell: ({ getValue }) => <Badge size="sm">{getValue<string>()}</Badge>,
  },
  {
    accessorKey: "balance",
    header: "Balance",
    meta: { numeric: true },
    cell: ({ getValue }) => `$${getValue<number>()}`,
  },
]

export function MembersTable({ data }: { data: Member[] }) {
  return <DataTable columns={columns} data={data} />
}
```

## Density

Like other Koala surfaces, Code Snippet honors `density`. `compact` (the default) suits dense app UI; `comfortable` opens up the padding for docs and marketing. Density retunes spacing only, never radius or color.

```tsx title="comfortable.tsx"
const theme = "moonlight"
```

```tsx title="compact.tsx"
const theme = "moonlight"
```

## API reference

### CodeSnippet

A highlighted, copyable code block with a copy button on hover. Forwards native `<div>` props except `children`; accepts `className`, merged last onto the root.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| code* | string | - | The source to render and copy. |
| lang | string | "tsx" | The language and the header chip. TSX, TS, JS, JSON, CSS and shell are built in; a shell listing with `$` prompts reads as a session. Any other language needs a `CodeHighlighterProvider`, or reads as plain text; `text` is always plain. |
| filename | string | - | A filename chip in the header (and turns the header on). |
| dots | boolean | false | macOS-style window dots in the header (and turns the header on). |
| inset | boolean | true | With a header: a tinted frame with the code set 8px in as a sheet. `false` makes it a strip across one surface. |
| showLineNumbers | boolean | false | A tabular line-number gutter. |
| startLine | number | 1 | The first gutter number, for an excerpt; `diff` uses the same numbering. |
| diff | { added?: number[]; removed?: number[] } | - | Lines marked by gutter number: a tinted band and gutter bar, announced as Added or Removed. |
| collapsible | boolean | false | Clamps a long listing behind Show more / Show less, once it overflows. |
| collapsedHeight | number | 320 | The clamped height in px. |
| density | "comfortable" \| "compact" | "compact" | Padding only. Falls back to the nearest `DensityProvider`. |

| Data attribute | Description |
| --- | --- |
| data-diff | `"added"` or `"removed"` on a marked line and its gutter cell. |

### CodeHighlighterProvider

From `@/lib/code-highlighter`. Every Code Snippet below it asks this highlighter first and falls back on its own grammar when the answer is `null`. Shell sessions keep the built-in reading.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| highlighter* | (code: string, lang: string) => CodeToken[][] \| null \| Promise<CodeToken[][] \| null> | - | Lines of `{ type?, value }` tokens, where `type` is a Koala syntax role. While a block streams, finished lines keep their color between answers. |

## FAQ

### Which languages does the highlighter support?

Out of the box, a small dependency-free tokenizer highlights TS/TSX, JS, JSON, shell and CSS. Any other language reads as plain text until you provide a highlighter: with the Shiki adapter above, every language Shiki bundles is highlighted in your theme's syntax colors.

### Does Shiki make the bundle bigger?

Only if you provide it. Code Snippet never imports Shiki; the adapter does, and it loads each language the first time a snippet uses it. Without a CodeHighlighterProvider nothing changes.

### Can I use Prism or my own highlighter?

Yes. A highlighter is a function (code, lang) that returns lines of { type, value } tokens, or a promise of them, or null for a language it does not know. The type is one of Koala's syntax roles: keyword, string, comment, function, number, tag, attribute or punctuation.

### How do I get the window chrome header?

Pass a filename to add the header with a language chip, and add the dots prop for macOS-style window dots. The header sits on a tinted frame with the code inset 8px as a sheet. Omit both for a chromeless block.

### Why does my snippet show a frame inside a frame?

It is already a sheet of another frame, like a preview's Code tab. Pass inset={false} and the header becomes a strip across the one surface instead of a second frame.

### How do I show a command and its output?

Use lang="bash" and start each command line with "$ ". Lines without the prompt read as output in muted ink, and the copy button copies only the commands.

### Will the syntax colors follow my theme?

Yes. Highlighting is driven by syntax tokens (CSS variables), so the code re-themes across all four palettes rather than using fixed colors. Density retunes spacing only, never radius or color.

### How do I add a line-number gutter?

Set showLineNumbers to render a tabular-nums gutter, useful for longer listings or when referencing a specific line.

### Can it show a diff?

Yes. Pass diff with the added and removed line numbers, and startLine when the snippet is an excerpt, so the gutter and the marks use the file's real numbering. Marked lines get a soft green or red band and a gutter bar, and are announced as Added or Removed.

### How do I collapse a long code block?

Set collapsible to clamp the block to collapsedHeight (320px by default). The last lines fade into the surface and a Show more / Show less toggle expands it to full height. The toggle only shows up once the content actually overflows the clamp, so short blocks stay untouched.

### There are two CodeSnippets in Koala. Which import do I use?

For app code use the component at @/components/ui/code-snippet. The @/components/docs/code-snippet import is a docs-site wrapper used by these pages.

### Is there a copy button?

Yes. The block shows a copy-on-hover control that copies the exact code string you pass, so consumers can grab it without selecting text.

`npx koalaui-cli@latest add code-snippet` writes `components/ui/code-snippet/`. Import from `@/components/ui/code-snippet`:

- Components and helpers: `CodeSnippet`, `codeSnippetVariants`
- Types: `CodeSnippetProps`
- Koala components it installs with it: `animated-label`, `button`
